ticket.summary: Active water pouring through dining room ceiling light fixture from upstairs bathroom (suspected toilet); customer's toilet angle stop was seized, main shutoff located at water heater in garage and closed — flow stopped, on-call tech dispatched.
mitigation_advice: Do not touch the light fixture or standing water; shut off the dining room lighting breaker (water through an energized fixture)
Attempted toilet angle stop behind toilet — seized; advised NOT to force it to avoid snapping the valve
Advised holding/wedging the tank flapper closed and lifting the fill valve float as an interim stop
Located and closed main shutoff lever at water heater in garage (quarter turn, crosswise)
Opened lowest-floor cold faucet (kitchen sink) to depressurize and drain lines — ceiling drip reduced significantly
Keep bucket in place for residual trapped water; move furniture and rugs clear
Checked for ceiling bulge/sag — none present, ceiling wet only, no relief puncture needed
Photograph/video ceiling and wet area for insurance
No fixture use or flushing until tech restores water

quote_lines.description: After-hours emergency call-out, includes trip and on-site diagnosis (firm)
Estimated replacement of seized toilet angle stop, $145-185 range, to be confirmed on site before work

ticket.customer_message: You've earned that bucket-sitting break. Here's where we stand: Tech is en route - ETA ~35-45 min from now. He'll call your cell (+1-555-0104) when he's close. Keep the dining room breaker off until he clears the fixture, and leave the house water off until he restores it. He'll find the source upstairs, quote the repair before touching anything, and can dry-check the ceiling cavity so you know what your insurance is dealing with. You're all set - text back if anything changes before he arrives.
